It gives school students a chance to turn ideas into working prototypes and present them to industry mentors and judges. Website: Submission Will be updated soon Eligibility School students of Class 9th, 10th , 11th, 12th Team size: [2-4] members, all from the same school Registration through Unstop Format Round 1 (Online): Teams submit a short idea presentation (5 slides) and a 1-2 minute demo video. Coding is not compulsory; simple prototypes are welcome. Problem statements will be shared when the online round begins. Round 2 (Offline Finale): Top shortlisted teams build and present their prototypes at the Echelon campus in a 9-hour on-site round, with mentor support, lunch and a final 5-minute pitch. raw.details:
About the Event

EchelonHacks Young Innovators 2026 is an inter-school hackathon hosted by Echelon Institute of Technology, Faridabad (Dept. of Computer Science & Engineering). It gives school students a chance to turn ideas into working prototypes and present them to industry mentors and judges.

Website: Submission 
Will be updated soon

Eligibility

  • School students of Class 9th, 10th , 11th, 12th
  • Team size: [2-4] members, all from the same school
  • Registration through Unstop

Format

  • Round 1 (Online): Teams submit a short idea presentation (5 slides) and a 1-2 minute demo video. Coding is not compulsory; simple prototypes are welcome. Problem statements will be shared when the online round begins.
  • Round 2 (Offline Finale): Top shortlisted teams build and present their prototypes at the Echelon campus in a 9-hour on-site round, with mentor support, lunch and a final 5-minute pitch.

Timeline

  • Registration: 12 Oct - 30 Oct 2026
  • Online Round: 31 Oct - 5 Nov 2026
  • Results: 10 Nov 2026
  • Offline Finale: 21 Nov 2026, 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM, Echelon Institute of Technology, Faridabad

Judging Criteria
Idea and Innovation, Technical Feasibility, Real-World Impact, Presentation

Rules

  • Work must be original; plagiarism leads to disqualification
  • AI tools may be used for learning, but the team must be able to explain its own work
  • Shortlisted teams must submit a parent/guardian consent form and be accompanied by a teacher or guardian on finale day
  • Judges’ decisions are final
